Aisha: Heads-up — I opened a PR to unify the SDK code snippets for streaming + pagination across py/ts/go. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1104
Tom: Thanks. Which snippets are out of date?
Aisha: Mostly docs/reference/sdk/streaming.md and a couple includes in examples/includes/.py and .ts. Python still shows the old iterator pattern; TS uses the deprecated helper.
Riley: Can we pick one canonical pattern per language? My suggestion: Python sync uses client.responses.paginate() + client.responses.stream(cursor) (clear cursor variable), TS uses for-await-of client.responses.stream(cursor) inside paginate(), Go exposes a small helper returning a channel.
Aisha: Agreed. Also add a short retry helper (no external deps) and a note about idempotency keys for non-idempotent create() calls. Keep examples tiny.
Tom: I can patch the test harness that extracts snippets to ensure we validate both the displayed output and that examples compile (TS) / import (Py).
ci-bot: Preview build: https://deploys.redwood.dev/preview/5209 — results: 1 error (include not found: includes/examples/old_stream_py.md), 7 warnings.
Aisha: I'll remove the old include and replace it with a small sync + async Python snippet. Draft Python snippet inline:
```
from redwood import Redwood
import time, random
client = Redwood()

def simple_backoff(fn, attempts=4):
    for i in range(attempts):
        try:
            return fn()
        except Exception:
            time.sleep(min(2**i + random.random(), 8))
    raise

# streaming + pagination (sync)
for page in client.responses.paginate(model='rw-small', page_size=2):
    for chunk in client.responses.stream(page.cursor):
        print(getattr(chunk, 'text', '') or getattr(chunk, 'delta', ''))

# create() with retries and idempotency key
resp = simple_backoff(lambda: client.responses.create(model='rw-small', input='hi', idempotency_key='op-123'))
print(resp)
```
Riley: TS snippet I'd push:```
for await (const page of client.responses.paginate({ model: 'rw-small', page_size: 2 })) {
  for await (const part of client.responses.stream(page.cursor)) {
    console.log(part.delta ?? part.text)
  }
}
```
Riley: For Go I'll add a StreamWithPagination helper in includes so the main doc shows only 3 lines. Keeps cursor handling out of readers' hair.
Tom: Pushed tests update to accept both sync/async py snippets. Left one nit about variable names and a comment.
Aisha: Fixed the include paths and added the docs-bot suggestion: one-line warning about preserving cursor state across pages to avoid double consumption and duplicate billing.
docs-bot: Suggested wording: "Persist the cursor between pages; re-requesting a completed cursor can re-deliver tokens and incur duplicate charges."
ci-bot: Re-run preview: https://deploys.redwood.dev/preview/5216 — build green, 3 warnings (markdown lint).
Tom: Looks good. I'll merge and backport a tiny changelog entry to docs/changelog/2026-03.md explaining the snippet harmonization and the retry/idempotency note.
Riley: Filed follow-up GH issue to update snippet unit tests to assert presence of the idempotency example for non-idempotent calls.
Aisha: Thanks team — will add a short FAQ blurb in docs/migration/2026-streaming.md about long-running streams and cursor persistence. :thumbsup:
